newsitem.title: KENYA: Man beaten to death at Kenya opposition rally.
newsitem.headline: Man beaten to death at Kenya opposition rally.

text.p: A man suspected of being a police spy was beaten to death at an opposition rally in Nairobi on Friday, a spokesman for a medical charity said.
Said Athman, a spokesman for the medical charity St Johns, told Reuters the man identified as Gilbert Ahanya Simiyu was pronounced dead on arrival at Nairobi hospital at around 12 p.m. (0900 GMT).
Barely 1,000 activists turned up for the rally in Nairobi's Uhuru park to hear opposition speakers demand sweeping political reforms from President Daniel arap Moi before elections due this year.
Witnesses said Simiyu was beaten by a mob shortly after the rally started. Oppostion supporters said he was from the police special branch division but police could not confirm or deny the report.
Two other people were also lynched but they fled and were not in any serious physical danger, witnesses said.

Most city centre shops were closed and some workers stayed at home. But shop-owners, many from the vulnerable Asian community, said they closed for fear of the violence and looting which mar political demonstrations in Kenya.
